purpose: Provide a frozen relationship-phenotype vocabulary for narrative classification. The registry separates actor-specific experience, dyadic interaction, time trajectory, and context so relationship history is not collapsed into a compatibility score.
global_rules: Never compute an overall compatibility score from these axes.
Classify Person A toward Person B and Person B toward Person A separately whenever the construct can differ by actor.
Preserve unknown, mixed, and context-dependent states rather than forcing a midpoint.
Behavioral constraint is not the same as internal desire: religion, virginity, health, distance, language, opportunity, trauma, and relationship agreements may reduce observability.
Visible drama is not equivalent to serious conflict or internal emotional dysregulation.
Love/attachment, Eros/in-love, physical attraction, sexual desire, and commitment are distinct constructs.
Intellectual compatibility, intellectual stimulation, conceptual comprehension, shared interests, communication quality, and communication abundance are distinct constructs.
Mystical/spiritual salience is distinct from mystical curiosity/inquiry.
Record trajectories and state curves when a relationship changes with familiarity, distance, cohabitation, attachment threat, or third-party relationships.

axes.definition: How physically attractive the actor experiences the partner, independent of libido or sexual satisfaction.
How strongly the actor wants sexual contact with this partner, independent of behavior constraints.
How often the actor initiates sexual contact relative to available opportunities; do not infer desire from initiation alone.
General sexual appetite across partners/contexts, separated from attraction to this partner.
How satisfying/enjoyable the sexual interaction is for the actor when it occurs.
Observed fit of the sexual system as a pair; must reflect both actors, desire match, responsiveness, and actual experience.
How well partner-specific desire persists as familiarity increases.
Tendency for sexual response to decline with familiar partners and revive with novelty/new partners.
Romantic in-love state: longing, romantic specialness, desire for romantic reciprocity and priority; distinct from love/attachment.
Strength of enduring affection/attachment independent of whether the actor is romantically in love.
Friendship-like or familial companionate affection distinct from erotic/romantic Eros.
Desire/intention to maintain, formalize, marry, or build a durable life with the partner.
How much the actor can confide, disclose, and feel psychologically known/safe with the partner.
How well the actor can know what the partner is feeling/thinking; separate from the partner's internal emotional ease.
How understood, validated, cared for, and appropriately responded to the actor feels.
Ease and quality of sustained reasoning together, productive disagreement, mutual comprehension, and building ideas together.
How much the partner surprises, expands, catalyzes, or changes the actor's thinking.
Observed speed/quality of understanding difficult concepts and applying them effectively; not equivalent to conversational output.
How experientially salient religion, spirituality, intuition, mystical phenomena, dreams, ritual, or metaphysical interpretation are.
How strongly the person actively investigates, questions, learns about, or seeks mystical/spiritual ideas and practices.
How much the partner expands or energizes the actor's spiritual/mystical thinking or practice.
Clarity, honesty, reasoning quality, and ability to understand one another when communicating.
Amount/continuity of meaningful communication; separate from quality.
Amount and depth of genuinely shared interests/activities/worldview material.
How much the partner contributes useful knowledge the actor lacks without necessarily being globally stimulating.
Frequency/intensity of expressive, theatrical, playful, or emotionally demonstrative episodes, regardless of hostility.
Frequency/intensity of hostile conflict, coercion, aggression, contempt, or serious relational rupture.
How much effort/time is required to return to functional connection after conflict; higher means harder repair.
How emotionally settled/easy the relationship feels to the actor internally; may remain unknown when observability is poor.
Freedom to remain oneself, have independent goals/relationships/time, and spend time apart without punishment.
Pressure to merge, attend, reassure, sacrifice, or organize life around the relationship beyond what the actor freely wants.
Distress/constraint around the partner having sexual contact with others.
Distress around the partner falling in love with, prioritizing, or reallocating substantial romantic attention to another person.
How strongly closeness, cohabitation, frequent contact, or attachment activation increases pressure/conflict/jealousy.
Reliability, honesty, interpersonal safety, and expectation that the partner will not exploit vulnerability.
Practical/emotional support, advocacy, willingness to help, and care for the partner's well-being.
Compatibility of geography, money, work, children/family, domestic life, religion, community, relationship structure, lifestyle, and future plans.
